title: Optical Transceiver Suppliers: Who Makes Each Part After NVIDIA's $4 Billion Bet
content:
On March 2, 2026, NVIDIA announced $2 billion investments each in Lumentum and Coherent, $4 billion in total. Neither is a GPU company; both supply parts for optical transceivers, which turn electricity into light so AI servers can exchange data. Taking a transceiver apart, laser diodes come from Coherent and Lumentum, DSP chips from Broadcom and Marvell, optical fiber from Corning and finished modules from China's InnoLight. The only Korean company confirmed in the chain is OE Solutions, which makes the laser chip. Nationality was not a filter; only suppliers that could be confirmed are listed.

1. Why AI servers need optical transceivers

When AI servers exchange data, copper wire heats up and cannot carry signals far. So electricity is converted to light and sent through optical fiber, and the part that does the conversion is the optical transceiver.

2. What NVIDIA's $4 billion covers

Lumentum received $2 billion plus a purchase commitment worth several billion dollars and rights to future production capacity, and Coherent received $2 billion. Both companies said the money would expand U.S. production capacity and speed up optical R&D; no split by use per company was found. These are announced investments, and whether they have been fully carried out was not confirmed.

3. Laser diodes: Coherent and Lumentum

Laser diodes that turn electricity into light are led by Coherent and Lumentum, the two companies NVIDIA invested in.

4. DSP chips: Broadcom and Marvell

DSP chips, which restore distorted light signals by calculation, are estimated to be over 90% Marvell and Broadcom combined, with Marvell at about 60% and Broadcom at 30% or more. This is industry analysis, not a research firm's count, so no agency is named.

5. Optical fiber: Corning

Corning is the market leader in optical fiber. A specific share figure could not be confirmed from public data, so only its ranking is given. Its optical communications sales were $2.07 billion in the second quarter of 2026 (+32% year over year), and AI data center sales nearly doubled. It also has a long-term supply agreement with Meta of up to $6 billion through 2030.

6. Finished modules and contract assembly

InnoLight of China is first in finished modules, with an estimated 35–40% of 800G; estimates differ by source. Fabrinet is a contract assembler that does not sell under its own brand. It is incorporated in the Cayman Islands, headquartered in Thailand and listed in New York, so no single nationality is given. Fiscal 2026 customer shares were Cisco 19.9%, NVIDIA 16.3%, Nokia 10.7% and Amazon 10.5%. NVIDIA's share has fallen from 35.1% in fiscal 2024, so calling Fabrinet only an NVIDIA subcontractor no longer fits.

7. The Korean company: OE Solutions

OE Solutions was the first in Korea to develop a 100G EML laser diode chip, a part that accounts for about 30% of a transceiver's cost. The 100G class is already in mass production, while 200G and 400G classes are in customer sampling and qualification tests, so "developed" and "supplied in volume" are kept apart. It holds the top share of Korea's optical transceiver market, and its transceivers reach the U.S. through Ciena and Nokia.

8. CPO and who sold first

Co-packaged optics (CPO) removes the module and places the optical engine next to the chip. NVIDIA is the better-known face of CPO, but Broadcom sold first, shipping tens of thousands of Tomahawk 5-Bailly CPO switches in 2025. NVIDIA put Quantum-X Photonics out in early 2026 and set full production of Spectrum-X Ethernet Photonics for the second half of 2026. Both companies use TSMC's COUPE process.

What could and could not be confirmed

Confirmed: the NVIDIA investment announcement, the leading company for each part, OE Solutions' 100G production stage and Fabrinet's customer shares. Not confirmed: whether the investments were fully carried out, Corning's exact share, the customer list of RF Materials (not public, so the company is not named as a supplier) and the contents of Korean equipment makers' CPO orders. A small Korean optical supplier with three straight years of losses and 1.6T revenue still ahead was left out. The DSP share and InnoLight's share are industry analysis and estimates, not agency counts.

Quick FAQ

Why did NVIDIA invest $4 billion in non-GPU companies?
It announced on March 2, 2026 that it would invest $2 billion each in Lumentum and Coherent; both said the money would expand U.S. production and speed optical R&D. This is the announced amount, not confirmed disbursement.

Which Korean company is in an optical transceiver?
OE Solutions, which makes the laser chip. The 100G class is in mass production; 200G and 400G are in qualification tests.

Is Fabrinet just an NVIDIA subcontractor?
No. NVIDIA's share fell from 35.1% in fiscal 2024 to 16.3% in fiscal 2026, and the largest customer is now Cisco.

Did NVIDIA sell CPO first?
No. Broadcom shipped tens of thousands of CPO switches in 2025; NVIDIA's Quantum-X Photonics followed in early 2026.

Companies named are disclosed or reported suppliers; shares come from different sources and dates, include industry estimates, and may have changed. Images are reconstructions based on public information, not an actual teardown. Sources include the NVIDIA newsroom and CNBC (March 2, 2026), Optica OPN, optics.org, Broadcom, NVIDIA, TSMC, Corning's Q2 2026 results, Fabrinet's fiscal 2026 10-K, LightCounting and OE Solutions filings and reports.
